method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula/macro/reference comparison, reverse paraphrase and bounded primary-source terminology research; not independent or human review.
scope: All nineteen translated blocks in the Cauchy-sequence appendix, including the historical motivation, epsilon definitions, quotient construction, ordered-field statements and completeness proof sketch.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The alternative construction traces back to Cauchy's sequence condition and later nineteenth-century authors. Stevin's decimal view motivates encoding reals by increasingly accurate rational approximations, while an alternating zero-one sequence shows that arbitrary rational sequences are unsuitable.
samples.checks: All historical names and citations, four square-root occurrences, both decimal displays, the three-item encoding argument and both cases of the alternating function are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Because real quantification cannot be assumed while constructing the reals, a rational epsilon Cauchy condition is used. Different sequences can encode the same real; their difference tending to zero defines the equivalence relation and the reals are its equivalence classes.
samples.checks: Every quantifier, domain, absolute-value inequality, reference, zero-limit formula and exercise equation has exact structural parity. MRARITH-009 corrects relations to classes.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Constant rational sequences embed the rationals. Pointwise sum and product define operations on sequence classes, and eventual positivity defines order. These equivalence classes form an ordered field and satisfy a least-upper-bound statement.
samples.checks: Both operation equations, pointwise definitions, positivity quantifiers and theorem labels are retained. MRARITH-010 uses real zero, MRARITH-011 names the quotient carrier, and MRARITH-012 records the omitted representative-independence check.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A rational lower and upper bracket is bisected recursively. The resulting Cauchy sequences approach the same class; the decreasing upper sequence bounds S and the increasing lower sequence proves leastness.
samples.checks: The initial bounds, midpoint, both recursive cases, halving argument, reductio inequalities and leastness chain are all preserved exactly.

source_observations.finding: The source names equivalence relations where equivalence classes are required.
source_observations.resolution: The Marathi body uses तुल्यतावर्ग and documents the correction adjacent to the sentence.

source_observations.finding: The source compares a real class with rational zero in the positivity definition.
source_observations.resolution: The Marathi formula uses 0_Real and exact QA projects only that documented symbol back to the frozen source.

source_observations.finding: Several statements conflate Cauchy sequences with their equivalence classes.
source_observations.resolution: The field carrier is explicit in Marathi and an adjacent convention covers the proof's preserved representative shorthand.

source_observations.finding: Closure is assigned but representative independence of quotient operations is not.
source_observations.resolution: The missing well-definedness obligation is disclosed without inventing an omitted proof.

limitations: No independent linguistic or mathematical certification has been performed.
